prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Pearland, Texas, and has whiplash. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1199; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you reported in Pearland, Texas. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather just go by my first name for now, if that's okay.

Q: That's fine. Can you describe where you were driving when the collision happened?

A: I was heading down a two-lane road in the middle of the afternoon. Traffic was light, and I was going maybe twenty-five miles an hour because of a school zone.

Q: What happened next?

A: The other car drifted into my lane. I braked and turned, but we still ended up nose to nose. It didn't feel like a big hit, more like a hard jolt.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?

A: Yes, and the airbags didn't go off, if that matters.

Q: Did you feel any pain right away?

A: Not really at first. Around the next morning my neck got stiff, and by that evening I had a headache that kept spreading into my shoulders. Turning my head to check my mirrors is hard now.

Q: Have you seen a doctor since the collision?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic two days later. They gave me a neck brace and told me to follow up with a physical therapist.

Q: Do you have any prior injuries to your neck or back?

A: Nothing serious. I had some stiffness years ago after a fall, but I recovered fully and didn't need treatment.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add?

A: Only that I'm still having trouble sleeping because of the pain, and I want to make sure my treatment gets covered.

Q: Understood. We'll follow up with you about next steps. Thank you for your cooperation.
